name: a motion that is null
why: Only a JSON object is a motion.

name: a motion that is a list
why: A list is not an object, whatever it holds.

name: a motion that is a string
why: A string has a length in both languages and is still not an object.

name: the five fields alone
why: The motion every file before the grouping is: one part a joint, the last placed off first.

name: the five fields and a measured travel
why: A distance per part, more than none for every part with a heading.

name: runs and no sub-assemblies
why: Two caps pressed onto a tube at once come off at once.

name: a sub-assembly lifted off whole and then parted
why: A bracket and its pin come off along their shared heading, then the pin leaves the bracket.

name: two sub-assemblies in one run
why: Each comes off along its own members' shared heading, then each comes apart.

name: a sub-assembly that stays put and only comes apart
why: Its members have no heading in releases, so it only splits; a cover gives the motion a heading.

name: a sub-assembly that stays put and splits, with nothing else moving
why: Only a split would move, and at least one release slot has to be a heading.

name: a sub-assembly that comes off whole and never comes apart
why: Nothing asks a member to split: every split slot empty and every split travel 0.

name: an empty list of sub-assemblies beside steps
why: Present and empty is allowed once steps are there.

name: drawn parts listed out of order
why: The drawn ordinals are compared as a set; the order is the payload's to give.

name: no order
why: order is required.

name: an order missing a drawn part
why: order is as long as the parts drawn.

name: an order naming a part twice
why: order names each drawn part exactly once.

name: an order naming a part twice, once as 1.0
why: 1.0 is the part 1 to both readers, so part 1 is named twice and part 2 not at all.

name: an order naming a part not drawn
why: Part 3 is not drawn, and has no release slot either.

name: an order naming a part as true
why: Python's True equals 1 and would sort into place; a boolean is not an ordinal.

name: an order written as a string of digits
why: Three characters long, like the parts drawn, but not a list.

name: an order holding a list
why: An ordinal is a number, not a list holding one.

name: an order naming a part by an integer too long for a double
why: Python reads an int no float can hold and JavaScript reads Infinity; neither is a drawn part.

name: an order written as floats and with an exponent
why: Python reads 1.0 and 20e-1 as floats and JavaScript as integers; to both they are whole.

name: a drawn part with no release slot
why: Slots are indexed by ordinal, and two slots have no index 2.

name: nothing drawn and nothing to move
why: Every list fits a model of no parts, but no release slot is a heading.

name: no releases
why: releases is required.

name: a release slot missing
why: releases has a slot for every drawn part.

name: a release slot too many
why: releases has a slot for every drawn part and no more.

name: a heading of two numbers
why: A slot is empty or exactly three numbers.

name: a heading of four numbers
why: A slot is empty or exactly three numbers; a fourth is not ignored.

name: a release slot holding null
why: A part that stays is an empty list, not null.

name: a heading written as a three-character string
why: Three characters are not three numbers.

name: a heading written as an object with a length
why: An object with indices and a length is not a list.

name: a heading of booleans
why: Python reads False and True as 0 and 1; a boolean is not a number.

name: a heading holding a string
why: Text is not a number, though JavaScript would turn this one into 1 if asked.

name: a heading holding 1e400
why: Both readers turn 1e400 into infinity, which is not a finite number.

name: no release slot with a heading
why: Nothing would move.

name: the only heading exactly HEADING_EPSILON long
why: A length not above the threshold is no heading, so nothing would move.

name: the only heading just longer than HEADING_EPSILON
why: Above the threshold is a heading, however short.

name: no stretch beside a travel
why: stretch is required, even where a travel leaves it unused.

name: a stretch slot missing
why: stretch has an entry for every drawn part.

name: a stretch of zero
why: A stretch is at least 1.

name: a stretch as large as the part count
why: A stretch may be as large as the part count.

name: a stretch past the part count
why: A stretch is at most the part count.

name: a stretch that is a fraction
why: A stretch is a whole number.

name: a stretch written as 2.0
why: A float to Python and an integer to JavaScript; to both, the whole number 2.

name: a stretch of true
why: Python's True is 1, inside the range; a boolean is not a number.

name: a stretch of 1e308
why: A whole number to both readers, and far past the part count.

name: a stretch holding a list
why: A list holding a number is not a number.

name: no explode_fraction beside a travel
why: explode_fraction is required, even where a travel leaves it unused.

name: an explode_fraction of zero
why: The fraction is above 0.

name: an explode_fraction of one
why: The fraction may be as large as MAX_EXPLODE_FRACTION.

name: an explode_fraction just above one
why: The next double above MAX_EXPLODE_FRACTION is past it.

name: an explode_fraction of true
why: Python's True is 1, inside the range; a boolean is not a number.

name: an explode_fraction written as a string
why: Text is not a number, though JavaScript's isFinite says this one is.

name: an explode_fraction wrapped in a list
why: A list is not a number, though JavaScript's isFinite says this one is.

name: an explode_fraction of 1e308
why: Finite, and far past MAX_EXPLODE_FRACTION.

name: an explode_fraction of 1e400
why: Both readers turn 1e400 into infinity, which is not a finite number.

name: an explode_fraction that is an integer too long for a double
why: Python reads an int no float can hold and JavaScript reads Infinity; neither is finite.

name: an explode_fraction so small it reads as zero
why: Both readers round 1e-400 to 0, which is not above 0.

name: the smallest explode_fraction a double holds
why: The smallest double is above 0.

name: a travel holding null
why: Only an absent travel falls back to the spacing; one that is there holds a list.

name: a travel that is not a list
why: travel is a list of distances.

name: a travel slot missing
why: travel has an entry for every drawn part.

name: a negative travel
why: A travel is at least 0.

name: no travel for a part with a heading
why: A part with a heading travels more than none.

name: a travel for a part that stays
why: Only a part with a heading needs more than none; one that stays may carry any travel in range.

name: a travel at the cap
why: Three parts times MAX_TRAVEL_PER_PART, as both sides compute the product.

name: a travel just past the cap
why: The next double above the cap is past it.

name: a travel of false for a part that stays
why: Python's False equals the 0 a part that stays may travel; a boolean is not a number.

name: a travel written as a string
why: Text is not a distance.

name: a travel holding an object
why: An object is not a distance.

name: steps holding null
why: Only an absent steps makes each part a run of its own; one that is there holds runs.

name: steps that are not a list
why: An object keyed by position is not a list of runs.

name: steps written as the order itself
why: Each run is a list; a bare ordinal is not a run of one.

name: an empty list of steps
why: No runs add up to no order.

name: an empty run
why: A run is never empty.

name: runs leaving a part out
why: The runs add up to the whole order.

name: runs naming a part twice
why: The runs add up to the order exactly, each part once.

name: runs out of the order's sequence
why: The runs keep the order's sequence, not only its parts.

name: runs cut at other places in the order's sequence
why: Where the order is cut is free, as long as the runs add up to it.

name: a run naming a part as false
why: Python's False equals 0, the order's first part; a boolean is not an ordinal.

name: runs written with integral floats
why: 0.0, 1.0 and 2.0 are the parts 0, 1 and 2 to both readers.

name: a run holding a nested list
why: A run holds ordinals, not lists of them.

name: sub-assemblies without steps
why: A sub-assembly is parts of one run, so steps have to be there.

name: an empty list of sub-assemblies without steps
why: The key asks for steps even when it lists nothing.

name: sub-assemblies holding null
why: A key that is there holds a list.

name: sub-assemblies given as one object
why: Even one sub-assembly is given in a list.

name: a sub-assembly that is a list of parts
why: Each sub-assembly is an object.

name: a second sub-assembly that is null
why: Every entry is an object, not only the first.

name: a sub-assembly naming no parts
why: A sub-assembly lists its parts.

name: a sub-assembly of one part
why: A sub-assembly has two parts or more.

name: a sub-assembly naming a part twice
why: A sub-assembly's parts are distinct.

name: a sub-assembly naming a part twice, once as 1.0
why: 1 and 1.0 are one part to both readers.

name: a sub-assembly naming a part as true
why: Python's True equals 1, a part of the run; a boolean is not an ordinal.

name: a sub-assembly naming a part not drawn
why: Part 3 is in no run.

name: a sub-assembly holding a nested list
why: A member is an ordinal, not a list of one.

name: a sub-assembly across two runs
why: A sub-assembly's parts go on in one run.

name: a part in two sub-assemblies
why: Sub-assemblies share no part.

name: a sub-assembly written with integral floats
why: 1.0 and 2.0 are the parts 1 and 2 to both readers.

name: a sub-assembly with no splits
why: A sub-assembly lists its splits.

name: a split slot missing
why: splits has a slot for every member.

name: a split of two numbers
why: A split slot is empty or exactly three numbers.

name: a split slot holding null
why: A member that stays with the rest is an empty list, not null.

name: a split of booleans
why: Python reads False and True as 0 and 1; a boolean is not a number.

name: a split too short to be a heading, with no split travel
why: Three numbers with no length to speak of are no split heading, so the member travels 0.

name: a split too short to be a heading, with a split travel
why: No split heading, so the split travel has to be exactly 0.

name: a sub-assembly with no split travel
why: A sub-assembly lists its split travel.

name: a split travel slot missing
why: split_travel has an entry for every member.

name: a negative split travel
why: A split travel is at least 0.

name: a split travel at the cap
why: The cap is the model's part count times MAX_TRAVEL_PER_PART, not the sub-assembly's.

name: a split travel just past the cap
why: The next double above the cap is past it.

name: no split travel for a member that splits
why: A member with a split heading travels more than none.

name: a split travel for a member that stays
why: Unlike travel, a split travel is exactly 0 where there is no split heading.

name: a split travel of false for a member that stays
why: Python's False equals the 0 a member that stays travels; a boolean is not a number.

name: members leaving the model opposite ways
why: A sub-assembly comes off whole, so along one heading.

name: members of which only the first leaves the model
why: Either every member has a heading or none does.

name: members of which only the last leaves the model
why: Either every member has a heading or none does, whichever of them comes first.

name: members leaving the model the same way at different lengths
why: Headings are compared as directions, whatever their lengths.

name: members leaving the model a hair apart
why: About 5e-7 short of parallel, inside SAME_HEADING_TOLERANCE.

name: members leaving the model just too far apart
why: About 2e-6 short of parallel, outside SAME_HEADING_TOLERANCE.

name: members held to the first of them, not to one another
why: Each is within 4.1e-7 of the first, though the outer two are 1.6e-6 apart.

name: members held to a first at one edge of their spread
why: Measured from the first, the last is 1.6e-6 short of parallel.

name: members sharing a heading written in 1e308s
why: Its length is still finite, so it is the direction of 1, 1, 1.

name: members that stay, one empty and one too short to be a heading
why: Neither has a heading, which is none of them having one.

name: members of which one leaves and one is too short to be a heading
why: A heading too short to be one is none, beside a member that has one.

name: keys it does not know at the top level
why: Unknown keys are ignored, even ones named like a sub-assembly's.

name: a top-level key named __proto__
why: JSON makes it a key of its own to both readers, not a prototype the fields are read through.

name: keys it does not know in a sub-assembly, named like top-level ones
why: Unknown keys in an entry are ignored, even a travel and steps holding junk.

name: members sharing a heading of numbers too large to square
why: Three finite numbers have a length and a direction even where their squares overflow a double; both members point the same way.

name: a sub-assembly member with a heading and no travel of its own
why: The five fields stand on their own: a part with a heading travels, whatever the furthest member of its group travels.

name: members a hair outside the tolerance only when their dot product is summed x, y, z
why: Summed in the build's axis order the two headings fall just short of one direction; summed x, z, y they would not. Both checks sum x, y, z.

name: members a hair inside the tolerance only when their dot product is summed x, y, z
why: Summed in the build's axis order the two headings reach one direction; summed x, z, y they would fall just short. Both checks sum x, y, z.

name: a member's heading too large to square beside a short one the same way
why: Length does not change a direction, however long; the two members still come off as one.
